segments.src: > Growing a crop starts with three decisions — how you start the seed, whether you move the plant, and how tightly you pack the field — and those three choices set the ceiling on your harvest before the plant grows a single leaf.
segments.tr: > 작물을 키우는 것은 세 가지 결정에서 시작된다 — 씨앗을 어떻게 시작하는지, 식물을 옮기는지 여부, 그리고 밭을 얼마나 촘촘히 채우는지 — 그리고 이 세 가지 선택은 식물이 단 하나의 잎도 자라기 전에 수확량의 상한선을 정한다.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Every crop production system begins with the same question: **how do we get a plant from a seed into the ground, and how many of them do we want per acre?**
segments.tr: 모든 작물 생산 시스템은 같은 질문으로 시작된다: **씨앗에서 식물을 어떻게 땅에 심고, 에이커당 몇 개를 원하는가?**

segments.src: There are two basic routes.
segments.tr: 두 가지 기본 경로가 있다.

segments.src: **Direct seeding** means the seed goes straight into the field where the plant will finish its life.
segments.tr: **직파(직접 파종)**는 씨앗이 식물이 생을 마칠 밭으로 바로 들어간다는 뜻이다.

segments.src: Corn, soybeans, wheat, and carrots are almost always direct seeded.
segments.tr: 옥수수, 대두, 밀, 당근은 거의 항상 직파한다.

segments.src: It's cheap and fast — a planter can cover 40 acres an hour — but the seed is on its own out there, exposed to cold soil, crusting, birds, and weeds that germinate at the same time.
segments.tr: 비용이 저렴하고 빠르다 — 파종기는 시간당 40에이커를 커버할 수 있다 — 하지만 씨앗은 그곳에서 홀로 남겨져 찬 흙, 지각, 새, 동시에 발아하는 잡초에 노출된다.

segments.src: **Transplanting** means the seed germinates somewhere controlled — a greenhouse tray, a nursery bed — and the young plant is moved into the field later.
segments.tr: **이식(이앙)**은 씨앗이 통제된 어딘가 — 온실 트레이, 육묘상 — 에서 발아하고, 어린 식물이 나중에 밭으로 옮겨진다는 뜻이다.

segments.src: Tomatoes, peppers, broccoli, strawberries, and rice (in much of the world) go this route.
segments.tr: 토마토, 피망, 브로콜리, 딸기, 그리고 (세계의 많은 지역에서) 쌀은 이 경로를 간다.

segments.src: The controlled stage is called **raising seedlings**, or *nursery raising*.
segments.tr: 통제된 단계를 **묘목 육성**, 또는 *육묘*라고 한다.

segments.src: It costs far more per plant, but it buys you three things:
segments.tr: 식물당 훨씬 더 비싸지만, 세 가지를 얻는다:

segments.src: 1. **Time.** The seedling grows in a warm greenhouse in March while the field is still frozen. When you set it out in May, it's already five weeks old. In a short-season state like Minnesota, that's the difference between harvesting and not.
segments.tr: 1. **시간.** 묘목은 밭이 여전히 얼어있는 3월에 따뜻한 온실에서 자란다. 5월에 내보낼 때, 이미 5주 된 상태다. 미네소타처럼 짧은 계절의 주에서는, 수확과 하지 않는 것의 차이다.

segments.src: 2. **Uniformity.** You throw away the weak seedlings before they ever occupy field space. A direct-seeded field carries its runts all season.
segments.tr: 2. **균일성.** 약한 묘목을 밭 공간을 차지하기도 전에 버린다. 직파 밭은 약한 개체들을 전 시즌 동안 가져간다.

segments.src: 3. **A head start on weeds.** A four-week-old transplant shades out weed seedlings that a germinating direct-seeded crop would lose to.
segments.tr: 3. **잡초에 대한 선제 우위.** 4주 된 이식 묘목은 발아하는 직파 작물이 이기지 못할 잡초 묘목을 그늘지게 한다.

segments.src: The cost is **transplant shock** — roots get disturbed, the plant sulks for a few days.
segments.tr: 비용은 **이식 충격** — 뿌리가 방해받고, 식물이 며칠 동안 시들해진다.

segments.src: The standard fix is **hardening off**: a week or so of gradually exposing seedlings to outdoor cold, wind, and full sun so they toughen up before the move.
segments.tr: 표준 해결책은 **순화(경화)**: 묘목을 점진적으로 야외 추위, 바람, 햇빛에 노출시켜 옮기기 전에 단단해지도록 하는 일주일 정도의 기간이다.

segments.src: Then comes the third decision: **planting density** — how many plants per acre, and how they're arranged.
segments.tr: 그 다음은 세 번째 결정이다: **파종 밀도(식재 밀도)** — 에이커당 몇 개의 식물, 그리고 어떻게 배열되는가.

segments.src: This is the one that surprises people.
segments.tr: 이것이 사람들을 놀라게 하는 것이다.

segments.src: More plants does *not* mean more yield forever.
segments.tr: 더 많은 식물이 *절대* 더 많은 수확량을 의미하지 않는다.

segments.src: As you crowd plants together:
segments.tr: 식물을 촘촘히 모으면서:

segments.src: - **Yield per acre** rises, plateaus, and then falls (lodging, disease, shading).
segments.tr: - **에이커당 수확량**은 올라가다가, 정체하다가, 다시 떨어진다 (쓰러짐, 병, 그늘짐).

segments.src: - **Yield per individual plant** falls the whole way — steadily, from the very first added plant.
segments.tr: - **개별 식물당 수확량**은 내내 떨어진다 — 꾸준히, 맨 처음 추가된 식물부터.

segments.src: Which curve you optimize for depends on what you're selling.
segments.tr: 어느 곡선을 최적화하는지는 무엇을 팔고 있는가에 달려있다.

segments.src: If you sell by the ton — corn silage, hay, processing tomatoes — push density high and don't care that each plant is smaller.
segments.tr: 톤 단위로 팔면 — 옥수수 사일리지, 건초, 가공 토마토 — 밀도를 높이고 각 식물이 더 작다는 것을 신경 쓰지 마라.

segments.src: If you sell by the unit and size matters — a head of cabbage, a jack-o'-lantern pumpkin, a table-grade apple — back off, because a field of undersized product is worth less than a field of fewer good ones.
segments.tr: 단위 단위로 팔고 크기가 중요하면 — 배추 한 포기, 할로윈 호박, 테이블 등급 사과 — 줄여라, 왜냐하면 작은 제품이 가득한 밭이 적은 좋은 것들이 가득한 밭보다 가치가 적기 때문이다.

segments.src: The arrangement matters too, not just the count.
segments.tr: 배열도 중요하고, 단순한 개수만 아니다.

segments.src: The same 30,000 plants per acre can sit in 30-inch rows or 15-inch rows.
segments.tr: 같은 에이커당 30,000개의 식물이 30인치 열이나 15인치 열에 앉을 수 있다.

segments.src: Narrower rows spread plants into a more even, square-ish spacing, so each one competes less with its immediate neighbors and the canopy closes over the soil sooner — which shades out weeds and keeps moisture in.
segments.tr: 좁은 열은 식물을 더 균등하고 정사각형에 가까운 간격으로 퍼뜨리므로, 각각은 바로 옆 이웃과 덜 경쟁하고 수관이 흙 위로 더 빨리 덮인다 — 이는 잡초를 그늘지게 하고 수분을 유지한다.

segments.src: That's a big part of why US corn row spacing narrowed over the last century, alongside breeding for plants that tolerate crowding.
segments.tr: 이것이 미국 옥수수 열 간격이 지난 세기에 좁혀진 이유의 큰 부분이며, 혼잡을 견디는 식물을 위한 육종과 함께다.

segments.src: Rough shape of the relationship, in plain text:
segments.tr: 관계의 대략적인 형태, 평문으로:

segments.src: plants per acre = 43,560 / (row spacing in ft x in-row spacing in ft)
segments.tr: plants per acre = 43,560 / (row spacing in ft x in-row spacing in ft)

segments.src: So 30-inch rows (2.5 ft) with plants 7 inches apart in the row (0.583 ft) gives about 43,560 / 1.458 ≈ 29,900 plants per acre.
segments.tr: 따라서 30인치 열(2.5 ft)에서 열 내 7인치 간격의 식물(0.583 ft)은 약 43,560 / 1.458 ≈ 에이커당 29,900개 식물을 준다.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 일상 생활에서

segments.src: Walk through a garden center in Ohio in late April and you're looking at the whole lesson on two tables.
segments.tr: 4월 말 오하이오의 정원 센터를 거닐면, 두 테이블에서 전체 교훈을 보고 있다.

segments.src: On one table: seed packets.
segments.tr: 한 테이블에는: 씨앗 패킷.

segments.src: Beans, sweet corn, radishes, carrots — $2 to $4 a packet, dozens of seeds each.
segments.tr: 콩, 옥수수, 무, 당근 — 패킷당 $2~$4, 각각 수십 개의 씨앗.

segments.src: These are the direct-seed crops.
segments.tr: 이것들이 직파 작물이다.

segments.src: The packet says "sow directly outdoors after last frost" because these plants either grow fast enough not to need a head start (radishes, 25 days) or hate having their roots disturbed (carrots, beans).
segments.tr: 패킷에는 "마지막 서리 후 야외에 직접 파종"이라고 나와있다 왜냐하면 이 식물들은 충분히 빠르게 자라서 선제 우위가 필요 없거나(무, 25일) 뿌리가 방해받는 것을 싫어하기 때문이다(당근, 콩).

segments.src: On the other table: cell packs of tomato and pepper starts, $4 to $6 for a four-pack.
segments.tr: 다른 테이블에: 토마토와 피망 모종의 셀 팩, 4팩에 $4~$6.

segments.src: Nobody sells tomato seed packets to casual buyers with a straight face in Ohio, because a tomato seeded outdoors in May in Columbus won't ripen before the first fall frost.
segments.tr: 오하이오에서는 아무도 캐주얼 구매자에게 토마토 씨앗 패킷을 곧바로 팔지 않는다, 왜냐하면 5월에 콜럼버스에서 야외에 심은 토마토는 첫 번째 가을 서리 전에 익지 않기 때문이다.

segments.src: Somebody already did the nursery-raising work in February in a heated greenhouse — that's what you're paying for, and it's why a single tomato plant costs more than an entire packet of bean seed.
segments.tr: 누군가는 이미 2월에 데운 온실에서 육묘 작업을 했다 — 이것이 당신이 지불하는 것이고, 이것이 토마토 한 포기가 콩 씨앗 전체 패킷보다 비싼 이유다.

segments.src: Now the density part.
segments.tr: 이제 밀도 부분.

segments.src: Flip over that tomato tag: "space 24-36 inches apart."
segments.tr: 그 토마토 꼬리표를 뒤집어보라: "24~36인치 떨어져 심기."

segments.src: Most first-time gardeners ignore it and plant six tomatoes in a 4x4 raised bed, because the transplants look tiny and the bed looks empty.
segments.tr: 대부분의 처음 정원사는 이를 무시하고 4x4 높은 침대에 6개의 토마토를 심는다, 왜냐하면 이식 묘목이 작아 보이고 침대가 비어 보이기 때문이다.

segments.src: By August they've got a tangled mat with poor air circulation, more disease, and small fruit — a personal-scale demonstration of the yield-per-plant curve.
segments.tr: 8월까지 그들은 공기 순환이 나쁜 얽힌 매트, 더 많은 병, 그리고 작은 열매를 가지고 있다 — 개별 식물당 수확량 곡선의 개인 규모 시연.

segments.src: The commercial grower down the road faces the identical tradeoff, just with a spreadsheet: a processing tomato field headed for a cannery gets crowded hard, because the plant is selling by the ton.
segments.tr: 길 아래의 상업 재배자는 동일한 트레이드오프에 직면한다, 단지 스프레드시트로: 통조림 공장으로 향하는 가공 토마토 밭은 심하게 혼잡하게 된다, 왜냐하면 식물이 톤 단위로 팔리기 때문이다.

segments.src: A fresh-market field where big, blemish-free fruit brings a premium at the farmers market in Athens gets more room per plant.
segments.tr: 아테네의 농산물 직판장에서 큰, 흠이 없는 열매가 프리미엄을 가져오는 신선 시장 밭은 식물당 더 많은 공간을 얻는다.

segments.src: Same crop.
segments.tr: 같은 작물.

segments.src: Different market.
segments.tr: 다른 시장.

segments.src: Different correct density.
segments.tr: 다른 올바른 밀도.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 3줄 요약

segments.src: 1. Direct seeding puts seed straight in the field — cheap and fast; transplanting raises seedlings in a controlled nursery first — expensive, but it buys season length, uniformity, and a weed head start.
segments.tr: 1. 직파는 씨앗을 밭에 바로 심는다 — 싸고 빠름; 이식은 먼저 통제된 육묘장에서 묘목을 키운다 — 비싸지만, 계절 길이, 균일성, 잡초에 대한 선제 우위를 얻는다.

segments.src: 2. As planting density rises, yield per acre goes up then eventually down, while yield per individual plant declines the entire time — so the right density depends on whether your market pays by weight or by the size of each unit.
segments.tr: 2. 파종 밀도가 올라가면서, 에이커당 수확량은 올라갔다가 결국 떨어지고, 개별 식물당 수확량은 내내 감소한다 — 따라서 올바른 밀도는 시장이 무게로 지불하는지 각 단위의 크기로 지불하는지에 달려있다.

segments.src: 3. Arrangement matters alongside count: narrower rows spread the same plant population more evenly, reducing crowding between neighbors and closing the canopy sooner.
segments.tr: 3. 배열은 개수와 함께 중요하다: 좁은 열은 같은 식물 개체군을 더 균등하게 퍼뜨려, 이웃 간 혼잡을 줄이고 수관을 더 빨리 닫는다.

segments.tr: ## ✅ 자가 진단

segments.src: As you increase planting density, what happens to yield per individual plant?**
segments.tr: 파종 밀도를 늘리면, 개별 식물당 수확량에 무슨 일이 일어나는가?**

segments.src: - A) It rises, then falls
segments.tr: - A) 올라갔다가 떨어진다

segments.src: - B) It falls steadily throughout
segments.tr: - B) 내내 꾸준히 떨어진다

segments.src: - C) It stays flat until the field is overcrowded
segments.tr: - C) 밭이 과밀해질 때까지 평평하게 유지된다

segments.src: - D) It rises steadily throughout
segments.tr: - D) 내내 꾸준히 올라간다

segments.src: "Hardening off" refers to:**
segments.tr: "순화(경화)"는 다음을 의미한다:**

segments.src: - A) Letting soil dry and crust before planting
segments.tr: - A) 심기 전에 흙을 건조하고 지각이 되게 놔두기

segments.src: - B) Selecting only the strongest seeds before sowing
segments.tr: - B) 파종 전에 가장 강한 씨앗만 선택하기

segments.tr: - D) 이식 후 뿌리 주위의 흙을 다지기

segments.tr: O/X: 할로윈 장식 시장을 위해 호박을 생산하는 재배자는 일반적으로 통조림 채우기용 호박을 재배하는 자보다 더 높은 밀도로 심어야 한다.**

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Direct seeding** — sowing seed straight into the field where the crop will grow to maturity, with no nursery stage.
segments.tr: - **직파(직접 파종)** — 씨앗을 육묘 단계 없이 작물이 성숙할 때까지 자랄 밭에 바로 파종하기.

segments.src: - **Transplanting** — moving a plant started elsewhere (greenhouse, nursery bed) into its final field position.
segments.tr: - **이식(이앙)** — 다른 곳에서 시작한 식물(온실, 육묘상)을 최종 밭 위치로 옮기기.

segments.src: - **Nursery raising (seedling production)** — growing young plants under controlled conditions before field setting, to gain season length and uniformity.
segments.tr: - **육묘(묘목 생산)** — 계절 길이와 균일성을 얻기 위해 밭 심기 전에 통제된 조건 하에서 어린 식물을 재배하기.

segments.src: - **Hardening off** — gradually acclimating protected seedlings to outdoor cold, wind, and sun so they survive transplanting with less shock.
segments.tr: - **순화(경화)** — 보호된 묘목을 점진적으로 야외 추위, 바람, 햇빛에 적응시켜 이식을 적은 충격으로 견디게 하기.

segments.src: - **Planting density (plant population)** — the number of plants per unit area, usually stated as plants per acre.
segments.tr: - **파종 밀도(식재 밀도, 식물 개체군)** — 단위 면적당 식물의 개수, 보통 에이커당 식물로 표시.

segments.src: - **Transplant shock** — the temporary growth setback a plant suffers from root disturbance and environmental change during transplanting.
segments.tr: - **이식 충격** — 이식 중 뿌리 방해와 환경 변화로 인해 식물이 겪는 일시적 생장 둔화.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — B.** Yield per plant declines from the very first added competitor, because each plant gets a smaller share of light, water, and nutrients.
segments.tr: *답: **1 — B.** 개별 식물당 수확량은 맨 처음 추가된 경쟁자부터 감소한다, 왜냐하면 각 식물은 빛, 물, 영양분의 더 작은 몫을 얻기 때문이다.

segments.src: Yield per acre is the curve that rises then falls; the two are often confused.
segments.tr: 에이커당 수확량은 올라갔다가 떨어지는 곡선; 둘은 종종 혼동된다.

segments.src: **2 — C.** Greenhouse seedlings are soft and unacclimated; a week of gradual outdoor exposure thickens cuticles and toughens tissue so the move doesn't set them back.
segments.tr: **2 — C.** 온실 묘목은 부드럽고 적응되지 않은 상태; 일주일의 점진적인 야외 노출은 큐티클을 두껍게 하고 조직을 단단하게 하므로 이동이 그들을 후퇴시키지 않는다.

zh.title: [农业101 #6] 农民为什么会为六英寸的土地而争论

segments.src: > Growing a crop starts with three decisions — how you start the seed, whether you move the plant, and how tightly you pack the field — and those three choices set the ceiling on your harvest before the plant grows a single leaf.
segments.tr: > 种植农作物始于三个决定——如何播种、是否移动植物，以及你在田地里种得有多紧密——这三个选择在植物长出单片叶子之前就决定了你的收获上限。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今天的概念

segments.src: Every crop production system begins with the same question: **how do we get a plant from a seed into the ground, and how many of them do we want per acre?**
segments.tr: 每个农作物生产系统都始于同一个问题：**我们如何让植物从种子进入土壤，每英亩我们想要多少株？**

segments.src: There are two basic routes.
segments.tr: 有两条基本的方案。

segments.src: **Direct seeding** means the seed goes straight into the field where the plant will finish its life.
segments.tr: **直接播种**意味着种子直接进入植物将完成生命周期的田地。

segments.src: Corn, soybeans, wheat, and carrots are almost always direct seeded.
segments.tr: 玉米、大豆、小麦和胡萝卜几乎总是直接播种。

segments.src: It's cheap and fast — a planter can cover 40 acres an hour — but the seed is on its own out there, exposed to cold soil, crusting, birds, and weeds that germinate at the same time.
segments.tr: 这很便宜且快速——播种机每小时可覆盖40英亩——但种子独自在那里，暴露于寒冷的土壤、结皮、鸟类和在同一时间发芽的杂草。

segments.src: **Transplanting** means the seed germinates somewhere controlled — a greenhouse tray, a nursery bed — and the young plant is moved into the field later.
segments.tr: **移植**意味着种子在受控的地方发芽——温室托盘、苗圃地——年轻的植物稍后被移入田地。

segments.src: Tomatoes, peppers, broccoli, strawberries, and rice (in much of the world) go this route.
segments.tr: 番茄、辣椒、西兰花、草莓和水稻（在世界上的大多数地方）采用这条路线。

segments.src: The controlled stage is called **raising seedlings**, or *nursery raising*.
segments.tr: 受控阶段称为**培育幼苗**或*苗圃培育*。

segments.src: It costs far more per plant, but it buys you three things:
segments.tr: 每株植物的成本要高得多，但它为你提供三件事：

segments.src: 1. **Time.** The seedling grows in a warm greenhouse in March while the field is still frozen. When you set it out in May, it's already five weeks old. In a short-season state like Minnesota, that's the difference between harvesting and not.
segments.tr: 1. **时间。** 幼苗在三月的温暖温室里生长，而田地仍然冻结。当你在五月把它放出来时，它已经五周大了。在像明尼苏达州这样的短季节州，这是收获和不收获的区别。

segments.src: 2. **Uniformity.** You throw away the weak seedlings before they ever occupy field space. A direct-seeded field carries its runts all season.
segments.tr: 2. **一致性。** 你在较小的幼苗占据田间空间之前就把它们丢掉。直接播种的田地整个季节都要照顾较小的植物。

segments.src: 3. **A head start on weeds.** A four-week-old transplant shades out weed seedlings that a germinating direct-seeded crop would lose to.
segments.tr: 3. **杂草的领先优势。** 一个四周大的移植物会遮挡直接播种的正在萌发的作物会输给的杂草幼苗。

segments.src: The cost is **transplant shock** — roots get disturbed, the plant sulks for a few days.
segments.tr: 代价是**移植冲击**——根部受到干扰，植物会闷闷不乐好几天。

segments.src: The standard fix is **hardening off**: a week or so of gradually exposing seedlings to outdoor cold, wind, and full sun so they toughen up before the move.
segments.tr: 标准的解决方法是**锻炼**：大约一周的时间逐渐让幼苗暴露于户外的寒冷、风和充足的阳光，使它们在移动前变得坚韧。

segments.src: Then comes the third decision: **planting density** — how many plants per acre, and how they're arranged.
segments.tr: 然后是第三个决定：**种植密度**——每英亩多少株植物，以及它们是如何排列的。

segments.src: This is the one that surprises people.
segments.tr: 这是让人们感到惊讶的。

segments.src: More plants does *not* mean more yield forever.
segments.tr: 更多的植物*不*意味着永远产量更多。

segments.src: As you crowd plants together:
segments.tr: 当你把植物挤在一起时：

segments.src: - **Yield per acre** rises, plateaus, and then falls (lodging, disease, shading).
segments.tr: - **单位面积产量**上升、保持稳定，然后下降（倒伏、病害、遮阴）。

segments.src: - **Yield per individual plant** falls the whole way — steadily, from the very first added plant.
segments.tr: - **单株产量**一直下降——从第一株添加的植物开始，持续下降。

segments.src: Which curve you optimize for depends on what you're selling.
segments.tr: 你优化哪条曲线取决于你在销售什么。

segments.src: If you sell by the ton — corn silage, hay, processing tomatoes — push density high and don't care that each plant is smaller.
segments.tr: 如果你按吨销售——玉米青贮、干草、加工番茄——推高密度，不在乎每株植物都较小。

segments.src: If you sell by the unit and size matters — a head of cabbage, a jack-o'-lantern pumpkin, a table-grade apple — back off, because a field of undersized product is worth less than a field of fewer good ones.
segments.tr: 如果你按单位销售且大小很重要——一棵卷心菜、一个南瓜灯、一个食用级苹果——退一步，因为一块尺寸不足的产品田不如一块少但优质的田值钱。

segments.src: The arrangement matters too, not just the count.
segments.tr: 排列方式也很重要，不仅仅是数量。

segments.src: The same 30,000 plants per acre can sit in 30-inch rows or 15-inch rows.
segments.tr: 相同的每英亩30,000株植物可以排列在30英寸行或15英寸行中。

segments.src: Narrower rows spread plants into a more even, square-ish spacing, so each one competes less with its immediate neighbors and the canopy closes over the soil sooner — which shades out weeds and keeps moisture in.
segments.tr: 较窄的行将植物分散到更均匀的、近似方形的间距，因此每株与其直接邻居的竞争较少，冠层更快地覆盖土壤——这可以遮挡杂草并保持水分。

segments.src: That's a big part of why US corn row spacing narrowed over the last century, alongside breeding for plants that tolerate crowding.
segments.tr: 这是美国玉米行距在过去一个世纪变窄的一个主要原因，以及为耐密集种植的植物选择育种的原因。

segments.src: Rough shape of the relationship, in plain text:
segments.tr: 关系的粗略形状，以纯文本形式：

segments.src: plants per acre = 43,560 / (row spacing in ft x in-row spacing in ft)
segments.tr: plants per acre = 43,560 / (row spacing in ft x in-row spacing in ft)

segments.src: So 30-inch rows (2.5 ft) with plants 7 inches apart in the row (0.583 ft) gives about 43,560 / 1.458 ≈ 29,900 plants per acre.
segments.tr: 所以30英寸的行距（2.5英尺）加上行内植物相隔7英寸（0.583英尺）大约给出43,560 / 1.458 ≈ 每英亩29,900株植物。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 在日常生活中

segments.src: Walk through a garden center in Ohio in late April and you're looking at the whole lesson on two tables.
segments.tr: 在4月下旬漫步通过俄亥俄州的一个花园中心，你会在两张桌子上看到整个课程。

segments.src: On one table: seed packets.
segments.tr: 在一张桌子上：种子包。

segments.src: Beans, sweet corn, radishes, carrots — $2 to $4 a packet, dozens of seeds each.
segments.tr: 豆类、甜玉米、萝卜、胡萝卜——每包2到4美元，每包数十粒种子。

segments.src: These are the direct-seed crops.
segments.tr: 这些是直接播种的作物。

segments.src: The packet says "sow directly outdoors after last frost" because these plants either grow fast enough not to need a head start (radishes, 25 days) or hate having their roots disturbed (carrots, beans).
segments.tr: 包装上说"最后霜冻后直接在户外播种"，因为这些植物要么生长得足够快，不需要提前开始（萝卜，25天），要么讨厌根部被打扰（胡萝卜、豆类）。

segments.src: On the other table: cell packs of tomato and pepper starts, $4 to $6 for a four-pack.
segments.tr: 在另一张桌子上：番茄和辣椒幼苗的细胞盘，四盒装4到6美元。

segments.src: Nobody sells tomato seed packets to casual buyers with a straight face in Ohio, because a tomato seeded outdoors in May in Columbus won't ripen before the first fall frost.
segments.tr: 在俄亥俄州，没有人能以直面的态度向普通买家销售番茄种子包，因为在哥伦布市5月在户外播种的番茄不会在第一次秋霜之前成熟。

segments.src: Somebody already did the nursery-raising work in February in a heated greenhouse — that's what you're paying for, and it's why a single tomato plant costs more than an entire packet of bean seed.
segments.tr: 有人已经在二月在加热的温室里做了苗圃培育工作——这就是你所支付的，这就是为什么单株番茄植物的成本比整包豆种更贵。

segments.src: Now the density part.
segments.tr: 现在讲讲密度的问题。

segments.src: Flip over that tomato tag: "space 24-36 inches apart."
segments.tr: 翻转那个番茄标签："相隔24-36英寸。"

segments.src: Most first-time gardeners ignore it and plant six tomatoes in a 4x4 raised bed, because the transplants look tiny and the bed looks empty.
segments.tr: 大多数首次园艺师忽视它，在4x4的高架床中种植六棵番茄，因为移植物看起来很小，床看起来是空的。

segments.src: By August they've got a tangled mat with poor air circulation, more disease, and small fruit — a personal-scale demonstration of the yield-per-plant curve.
segments.tr: 到八月，他们有了一个缠绕的一团，空气循环不良，疾病更多，果实较小——单株产量曲线的个人菜园演示。

segments.src: The commercial grower down the road faces the identical tradeoff, just with a spreadsheet: a processing tomato field headed for a cannery gets crowded hard, because the plant is selling by the ton.
segments.tr: 附近的商业种植者面临相同的权衡，只是使用电子表格：前往罐头厂的加工番茄田被挤得很紧，因为植物是按吨销售的。

segments.src: A fresh-market field where big, blemish-free fruit brings a premium at the farmers market in Athens gets more room per plant.
segments.tr: 一个新鲜市场田，其中大的、无瑕疵的果实在雅典农民市场获得溢价，每株植物获得更多空间。

segments.src: Same crop.
segments.tr: 相同的作物。

segments.src: Different market.
segments.tr: 不同的市场。

segments.src: Different correct density.
segments.tr: 不同的正确密度。

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 三行总结

segments.src: 1. Direct seeding puts seed straight in the field — cheap and fast; transplanting raises seedlings in a controlled nursery first — expensive, but it buys season length, uniformity, and a weed head start.
segments.tr: 1. 直接播种把种子直接放在田地里——便宜且快速；移植首先在受控的苗圃中培育幼苗——昂贵，但它购买季节长度、一致性和杂草领先优势。

segments.src: 2. As planting density rises, yield per acre goes up then eventually down, while yield per individual plant declines the entire time — so the right density depends on whether your market pays by weight or by the size of each unit.
segments.tr: 2. 当种植密度增加时，单位面积产量先上升然后最终下降，而单株产量始终下降——所以正确的密度取决于你的市场是按重量支付还是按每个单位的大小支付。

segments.src: 3. Arrangement matters alongside count: narrower rows spread the same plant population more evenly, reducing crowding between neighbors and closing the canopy sooner.
segments.tr: 3. 排列方式与数量同样重要：较窄的行更均匀地分散相同的植物数量，减少邻近植物之间的拥挤，更快地闭合冠层。

segments.tr: ## ✅ 自测

segments.tr: 当你增加种植密度时，单株产量会发生什么？**

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今天的术语

segments.src: - **Direct seeding** — sowing seed straight into the field where the crop will grow to maturity, with no nursery stage.
segments.tr: - **直接播种**——将种子直接播入田地，其中作物将成熟，没有苗圃阶段。

segments.src: - **Transplanting** — moving a plant started elsewhere (greenhouse, nursery bed) into its final field position.
segments.tr: - **移植**——将在其他地方开始的植物（温室、苗圃床）移动到其最终田间位置。

segments.src: - **Nursery raising (seedling production)** — growing young plants under controlled conditions before field setting, to gain season length and uniformity.
segments.tr: - **苗圃培育（幼苗生产）**——在田间设置前在受控条件下种植年轻植物，以获得季节长度和一致性。

segments.src: - **Hardening off** — gradually acclimating protected seedlings to outdoor cold, wind, and sun so they survive transplanting with less shock.
segments.tr: - **锻炼**——逐渐使受保护的幼苗适应户外寒冷、风和阳光，以便它们以较少冲击存活移植。

segments.src: - **Planting density (plant population)** — the number of plants per unit area, usually stated as plants per acre.
segments.tr: - **种植密度（植物数量）**——单位面积的植物数量，通常以每英亩植物数量表示。

segments.src: - **Transplant shock** — the temporary growth setback a plant suffers from root disturbance and environmental change during transplanting.
segments.tr: - **移植冲击**——植物在移植过程中由于根部干扰和环境变化而遭受的临时生长挫折。

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — B.** Yield per plant declines from the very first added competitor, because each plant gets a smaller share of light, water, and nutrients.
segments.tr: *答案：**1 — B.** 从第一个添加的竞争者开始，单株产量就下降了，因为每株植物获得更少的光、水和养分份额。

segments.src: Yield per acre is the curve that rises then falls; the two are often confused.
segments.tr: 单位面积产量是上升然后下降的曲线；两者经常被混淆。

segments.src: **2 — C.** Greenhouse seedlings are soft and unacclimated; a week of gradual outdoor exposure thickens cuticles and toughens tissue so the move doesn't set them back.
segments.tr: **2 — C.** 温室幼苗柔软且不适应；一周的逐渐户外暴露会增厚角质层并强化组织，使移动不会让它们回退。

segments.src: **3 — X (false).** It's the reverse.
segments.tr: **3 — 错（假）。** 这是相反的。

segments.src: Decorative pumpkins are sold by the unit and big fruit sells better, so they get more room per plant.
segments.tr: 装饰南瓜按单位销售，大果实销售更好，所以每株植物获得更多空间。

segments.src: Processing pumpkins are sold by weight to the cannery, where total tonnage per acre is all that matters, so they're planted more densely.*
segments.tr: 加工南瓜按重量销售给罐头厂，其中每英亩的总吨数是唯一重要的，所以它们的种植密度更高。*

segments.tr: हर फसल उत्पादन प्रणाली एक ही सवाल से शुरू होती है: **हम बीज से पौधे को जमीन में कैसे लाते हैं, और हम एक एकड़ में कितने चाहते हैं?**

segments.src: There are two basic routes.

segments.src: **Direct seeding** means the seed goes straight into the field where the plant will finish its life.

segments.src: Corn, soybeans, wheat, and carrots are almost always direct seeded.

segments.src: It's cheap and fast — a planter can cover 40 acres an hour — but the seed is on its own out there, exposed to cold soil, crusting, birds, and weeds that germinate at the same time.
segments.tr: यह सस्ता और तेज़ है — एक रोपण मशीन एक घंटे में 40 एकड़ को कवर कर सकती है — लेकिन बीज वहां अकेला होता है, ठंडी मिट्टी, पपड़ी, पक्षियों, और उन खरपतवारों के संपर्क में जो एक ही समय में अंकुरित होते हैं।

segments.src: **Transplanting** means the seed germinates somewhere controlled — a greenhouse tray, a nursery bed — and the young plant is moved into the field later.
segments.tr: **प्रत्यारोपण** का मतलब है कि बीज किसी नियंत्रित स्थान पर अंकुरित होता है — एक ग्रीनहाउस ट्रे, एक नर्सरी बेड — और युवा पौधे को बाद में खेत में स्थानांतरित किया जाता है।

segments.src: Tomatoes, peppers, broccoli, strawberries, and rice (in much of the world) go this route.
segments.tr: टमाटर, मिर्च, ब्रोकली, स्ट्रॉबेरी, और चावल (दुनिया के अधिकांश हिस्सों में) इस मार्ग से जाते हैं।

segments.src: The controlled stage is called **raising seedlings**, or *nursery raising*.
segments.tr: नियंत्रित चरण को **पौधरोपण** या *नर्सरी पालन* कहा जाता है।

segments.src: It costs far more per plant, but it buys you three things:
segments.tr: यह प्रति पौधे कहीं अधिक खर्चीला है, लेकिन यह आपको तीन चीजें देता है:

segments.src: 1. **Time.** The seedling grows in a warm greenhouse in March while the field is still frozen. When you set it out in May, it's already five weeks old. In a short-season state like Minnesota, that's the difference between harvesting and not.
segments.tr: 1. **समय।** मार्च में गर्म ग्रीनहाउस में पौध बढ़ता है जबकि खेत अभी भी जमा हुआ है। जब आप इसे मई में निकालते हैं, तो यह पहले से पाँच सप्ताह पुराना हो चुका है। मिनेसोटा जैसे अल्पकालीन मौसम वाले राज्य में, यह कटाई करने और न करने के बीच का अंतर है।

segments.src: 2. **Uniformity.** You throw away the weak seedlings before they ever occupy field space. A direct-seeded field carries its runts all season.
segments.tr: 2. **एकरूपता।** आप कमजोर पौधों को खेत की जगह लेने से पहले ही फेंक देते हैं। सीधी बुवाई वाला खेत पूरे मौसम में अपने बौने पौधों को ले जाता है।

segments.src: 3. **A head start on weeds.** A four-week-old transplant shades out weed seedlings that a germinating direct-seeded crop would lose to.
segments.tr: 3. **खरपतवारों पर आगे का दौड़।** एक चार सप्ताह पुराना प्रत्यारोपण खरपतवार के पौधों को छाया देता है जिन्हें अंकुरित सीधी बुवाई वाली फसल खो देगी।

segments.src: The cost is **transplant shock** — roots get disturbed, the plant sulks for a few days.
segments.tr: लागत **प्रत्यारोपण झटका** है — जड़ें बिगड़ जाती हैं, पौधा कुछ दिनों के लिए सुस्त हो जाता है।

segments.src: The standard fix is **hardening off**: a week or so of gradually exposing seedlings to outdoor cold, wind, and full sun so they toughen up before the move.
segments.tr: मानक समाधान **सख़्तता से तैयारी करना** है: लगभग एक सप्ताह पौधों को धीरे-धीरे बाहरी ठंड, हवा, और पूरी धूप के संपर्क में लाना ताकि वे स्थानांतरण से पहले मजबूत हो जाएं।

segments.src: Then comes the third decision: **planting density** — how many plants per acre, and how they're arranged.
segments.tr: फिर तीसरा निर्णय आता है: **रोपण घनत्व** — एक एकड़ में कितने पौधे, और वे कैसे व्यवस्थित हैं।

segments.src: This is the one that surprises people.
segments.tr: यह वही है जो लोगों को चौंकाता है।

segments.src: More plants does *not* mean more yield forever.
segments.tr: अधिक पौधे *नहीं* का मतलब हमेशा के लिए अधिक उपज नहीं है।

segments.src: As you crowd plants together:
segments.tr: जैसे-जैसे आप पौधों को एक साथ भीड़ते हैं:

segments.src: - **Yield per acre** rises, plateaus, and then falls (lodging, disease, shading).
segments.tr: - **प्रति एकड़ उपज** बढ़ती है, स्थिर हो जाती है, और फिर गिरती है (गिरना, रोग, छाया)।

segments.src: - **Yield per individual plant** falls the whole way — steadily, from the very first added plant.
segments.tr: - **प्रति पौधे की उपज** पूरी तरह गिरती है — लगातार, पहले से ही जोड़े गए पहले पौधे से।

segments.src: Which curve you optimize for depends on what you're selling.
segments.tr: आप किस वक्र को अनुकूलित करते हैं यह इस बात पर निर्भर करता है कि आप क्या बेच रहे हैं।

segments.src: If you sell by the ton — corn silage, hay, processing tomatoes — push density high and don't care that each plant is smaller.
segments.tr: यदि आप टन से बेचते हैं — मक्का का साइलेज, घास, प्रसंस्करण टमाटर — घनत्व को अधिक करें और इस बात की चिंता न करें कि प्रत्येक पौधा छोटा है।

segments.src: If you sell by the unit and size matters — a head of cabbage, a jack-o'-lantern pumpkin, a table-grade apple — back off, because a field of undersized product is worth less than a field of fewer good ones.
segments.tr: यदि आप इकाई से बेचते हैं और आकार महत्वपूर्ण है — गोभी का सिर, एक जैक-ओ-लालटेन कद्दू, एक टेबल-ग्रेड सेब — वापस लें, क्योंकि अंडरसाइज्ड उत्पाद का एक खेत कम अच्छे उत्पादों के खेत से कम मूल्य का है।

segments.src: The arrangement matters too, not just the count.
segments.tr: व्यवस्था भी महत्वपूर्ण है, केवल संख्या नहीं।

segments.src: The same 30,000 plants per acre can sit in 30-inch rows or 15-inch rows.
segments.tr: एक एकड़ में 30,000 पौधे 30-इंच पंक्तियों या 15-इंच पंक्तियों में बैठ सकते हैं।

segments.src: Narrower rows spread plants into a more even, square-ish spacing, so each one competes less with its immediate neighbors and the canopy closes over the soil sooner — which shades out weeds and keeps moisture in.
segments.tr: संकरी पंक्तियां पौधों को अधिक समान, वर्गाकार रिक्ति में फैलाती हैं, इसलिए प्रत्येक अपने तत्काल पड़ोसियों के साथ कम प्रतिस्पर्धा करता है और छतरी मिट्टी के ऊपर जल्दी बंद हो जाती है — जो खरपतवारों को छाया देता है और नमी को रखता है।

segments.src: That's a big part of why US corn row spacing narrowed over the last century, alongside breeding for plants that tolerate crowding.
segments.tr: यह इसका एक बड़ा हिस्सा है कि पिछली सदी में अमेरिकी मक्का की पंक्ति रिक्ति संकीर्ण क्यों हुई, भीड़ सहने वाले पौधों के प्रजनन के साथ।

segments.src: Rough shape of the relationship, in plain text:
segments.tr: संबंध का मोटा आकार, सादे पाठ में:

segments.src: plants per acre = 43,560 / (row spacing in ft x in-row spacing in ft)
segments.tr: plants per acre = 43,560 / (row spacing in ft x in-row spacing in ft)

segments.src: So 30-inch rows (2.5 ft) with plants 7 inches apart in the row (0.583 ft) gives about 43,560 / 1.458 ≈ 29,900 plants per acre.
## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## रोजमर्रा की जिंदगी में

segments.src: Walk through a garden center in Ohio in late April and you're looking at the whole lesson on two tables.
segments.tr: अप्रैल के अंत में ओहियो के एक बाग केंद्र से गुजरें और आप दो टेबलों पर पूरा पाठ देख रहे हैं।

segments.src: On one table: seed packets.
segments.tr: एक मेज पर: बीज के पैकेट।

segments.src: Beans, sweet corn, radishes, carrots — $2 to $4 a packet, dozens of seeds each.
segments.tr: बीन्स, मीठी मक्का, मूली, गाजर — $2 से $4 प्रति पैकेट, प्रत्येक में दर्जनों बीज।

segments.src: These are the direct-seed crops.
segments.tr: ये सीधे बीज वाली फसलें हैं।

segments.src: The packet says "sow directly outdoors after last frost" because these plants either grow fast enough not to need a head start (radishes, 25 days) or hate having their roots disturbed (carrots, beans).
segments.tr: पैकेट कहता है "अंतिम ठंढ के बाद सीधे बाहर बोएं" क्योंकि ये पौधे या तो तेजी से बढ़ते हैं कि उन्हें शुरुआत की जरूरत नहीं है (मूली, 25 दिन) या अपनी जड़ों को बिगड़ा हुआ देखना पसंद नहीं करते (गाजर, बीन्स)।

segments.src: On the other table: cell packs of tomato and pepper starts, $4 to $6 for a four-pack.
segments.tr: दूसरी मेज पर: टमाटर और मिर्च के शुरुआत के सेल पैक, $4 से $6 एक चार-पैक के लिए।

segments.src: Nobody sells tomato seed packets to casual buyers with a straight face in Ohio, because a tomato seeded outdoors in May in Columbus won't ripen before the first fall frost.
segments.tr: कोई भी ओहियो में आकस्मिक खरीदारों को गंभीर चेहरे के साथ टमाटर के बीज पैकेट नहीं बेचता है, क्योंकि कोलंबस में मई में बाहर बोया गया टमाटर पहली शरद ऋतु की ठंढ से पहले पक नहीं जाएगा।

segments.src: Somebody already did the nursery-raising work in February in a heated greenhouse — that's what you're paying for, and it's why a single tomato plant costs more than an entire packet of bean seed.
segments.tr: किसी ने पहले से ही फरवरी में एक गर्म ग्रीनहाउस में नर्सरी-पालन का काम किया है — यह वह है जिसके लिए आप भुगतान कर रहे हैं, और यह है कि एक एकल टमाटर के पौधे की लागत बीन के बीज के पूरे पैकेट से अधिक क्यों है।

segments.src: Now the density part.
segments.tr: अब घनत्व का हिस्सा।

segments.src: Flip over that tomato tag: "space 24-36 inches apart."
segments.tr: उस टमाटर टैग को पलटें: "24-36 इंच अलग स्पेस।"

segments.src: Most first-time gardeners ignore it and plant six tomatoes in a 4x4 raised bed, because the transplants look tiny and the bed looks empty.
segments.tr: अधिकांश पहली बार के माली इसे अनदेखा करते हैं और एक 4x4 ऊंचे बेड में छह टमाटर लगाते हैं, क्योंकि प्रत्यारोपण बहुत छोटे दिखते हैं और बेड खाली दिखता है।

segments.src: By August they've got a tangled mat with poor air circulation, more disease, and small fruit — a personal-scale demonstration of the yield-per-plant curve.
segments.tr: अगस्त तक उन्हें खराब वायु संचार, अधिक रोग, और छोटे फल के साथ एक उलझा हुआ मैट मिल गया है — उपज-प्रति-पौधे वक्र का एक व्यक्तिगत-पैमाने पर प्रदर्शन।

segments.src: The commercial grower down the road faces the identical tradeoff, just with a spreadsheet: a processing tomato field headed for a cannery gets crowded hard, because the plant is selling by the ton.
segments.tr: सड़क के नीचे वाणिज्यिक उत्पादक को समान व्यापार-बंद का सामना करना पड़ता है, बस एक स्प्रेडशीट के साथ: एक कैनरी के लिए जा रहा प्रसंस्करण टमाटर का खेत कठोर रूप से भीड़ हुआ है, क्योंकि पौधा टन से बेच रहा है।

segments.src: A fresh-market field where big, blemish-free fruit brings a premium at the farmers market in Athens gets more room per plant.
segments.tr: एक ताजा-बाजार खेत जहां बड़े, निर्दोष फल एथेंस के किसान बाजार में प्रीमियम लाते हैं प्रति पौधे अधिक जगह पाते हैं।

segments.src: Same crop.
segments.tr: एक ही फसल।

segments.src: Different market.
segments.tr: विभिन्न बाजार।

segments.src: Different correct density.
segments.tr: अलग सही घनत्व।

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## तीन-पंक्ति सारांश

segments.src: 1. Direct seeding puts seed straight in the field — cheap and fast; transplanting raises seedlings in a controlled nursery first — expensive, but it buys season length, uniformity, and a weed head start.
segments.tr: 1. सीधी बुवाई बीज को सीधे खेत में डालती है — सस्ता और तेज़; प्रत्यारोपण पहले एक नियंत्रित नर्सरी में पौधे उगाता है — महंगा, लेकिन यह मौसम की लंबाई, एकरूपता, और खरपतवार की शुरुआत खरीदता है।

segments.src: 2. As planting density rises, yield per acre goes up then eventually down, while yield per individual plant declines the entire time — so the right density depends on whether your market pays by weight or by the size of each unit.
segments.tr: 2. जैसे-जैसे रोपण घनत्व बढ़ता है, प्रति एकड़ उपज बढ़ती है फिर अंततः गिरती है, जबकि प्रति व्यक्तिगत पौधे की उपज पूरे समय गिरती है — इसलिए सही घनत्व इस बात पर निर्भर करता है कि आपका बाजार वजन से भुगतान करता है या प्रत्येक इकाई के आकार से।

segments.src: 3. Arrangement matters alongside count: narrower rows spread the same plant population more evenly, reducing crowding between neighbors and closing the canopy sooner.
segments.tr: 3. व्यवस्था संख्या के साथ मायने रखती है: संकरी पंक्तियां समान पौधे की आबादी को अधिक समान रूप से फैलाती हैं, पड़ोसियों के बीच भीड़ को कम करती हैं और छतरी को जल्दी बंद करती हैं।

segments.src: ## ✅ Self Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ स्व-प्रश्नोत्तरी

segments.src: As you increase planting density, what happens to yield per individual plant?**
segments.tr: जैसे-जैसे आप रोपण घनत्व बढ़ाते हैं, प्रति व्यक्तिगत पौधे की उपज को क्या होता है?**

segments.src: - A) It rises, then falls
segments.tr: - A) यह बढ़ता है, फिर गिरता है

segments.src: - B) It falls steadily throughout
segments.tr: - B) यह पूरी तरह लगातार गिरता है

segments.src: - C) It stays flat until the field is overcrowded
segments.tr: - C) यह समतल रहता है जब तक खेत भीड़ न हो जाए

segments.src: - D) It rises steadily throughout
segments.tr: - D) यह पूरे में लगातार बढ़ता है

segments.src: "Hardening off" refers to:**
segments.tr: "सख़्तता से तैयारी करना" निम्न को संदर्भित करता है:**

segments.src: - A) Letting soil dry and crust before planting
segments.tr: - A) रोपण से पहले मिट्टी को सूखने और पपड़ी बनाने देना

segments.src: - B) Selecting only the strongest seeds before sowing
segments.tr: - B) बोने से पहले केवल सबसे मजबूत बीज का चयन करना

segments.src: - C) Gradually exposing greenhouse seedlings to outdoor conditions before transplanting
segments.tr: - C) प्रत्यारोपण से पहले ग्रीनहाउस पौधों को धीरे-धीरे बाहरी परिस्थितियों के संपर्क में लाना

segments.src: - D) Compacting soil around the roots after transplanting
segments.tr: - D) प्रत्यारोपण के बाद जड़ों के चारों ओर मिट्टी को संपीड़ित करना

segments.src: O/X: A grower producing pumpkins for the Halloween decorative market should generally plant at a higher density than one growing pumpkins for canned filling.**
segments.tr: O/X: हैलोवीन सजावटी बाजार के लिए कद्दू का उत्पादन करने वाले एक उत्पादक को आमतौर पर डिब्बाबंद भरने के लिए कद्दू उगाने वाले से अधिक घनत्व पर रोपण करना चाहिए।**

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 आज की शर्तें

segments.src: - **Direct seeding** — sowing seed straight into the field where the crop will grow to maturity, with no nursery stage.
segments.tr: - **सीधी बुवाई** — बीज को सीधे खेत में बोना जहां फसल परिपक्वता तक बढ़ेगी, कोई नर्सरी चरण के बिना।

segments.src: - **Transplanting** — moving a plant started elsewhere (greenhouse, nursery bed) into its final field position.
segments.tr: - **प्रत्यारोपण** — किसी और जगह शुरू किए गए पौधे को (ग्रीनहाउस, नर्सरी बेड) इसकी अंतिम खेत स्थिति में ले जाना।

segments.src: - **Nursery raising (seedling production)** — growing young plants under controlled conditions before field setting, to gain season length and uniformity.
segments.tr: - **नर्सरी पालन (पौधरोपण उत्पादन)** — खेत सेट करने से पहले नियंत्रित परिस्थितियों में युवा पौधे उगाना, मौसम की लंबाई और एकरूपता प्राप्त करने के लिए।

segments.src: - **Hardening off** — gradually acclimating protected seedlings to outdoor cold, wind, and sun so they survive transplanting with less shock.

es.title: [Agriculture 101 #6] Por qué los agricultores luchan por seis pulgadas de tierra

segments.src: > Growing a crop starts with three decisions — how you start the seed, whether you move the plant, and how tightly you pack the field — and those three choices set the ceiling on your harvest before the plant grows a single leaf.
segments.tr: > Cultivar una cosecha comienza con tres decisiones — cómo se inicia la semilla, si se traslada la planta y cuán densamente se empaca el campo — y esas tres opciones establecen el techo de tu cosecha antes de que la planta crezca una sola hoja.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concepto de hoy

segments.src: Every crop production system begins with the same question: **how do we get a plant from a seed into the ground, and how many of them do we want per acre?**
segments.tr: Todo sistema de producción de cultivos comienza con la misma pregunta: **¿cómo pasamos una planta de una semilla al suelo, y cuántas queremos por acre?**

segments.src: There are two basic routes.
segments.tr: Hay dos rutas básicas.

segments.src: **Direct seeding** means the seed goes straight into the field where the plant will finish its life.
segments.tr: **La siembra directa** significa que la semilla va directamente al campo donde la planta terminará su vida.

segments.src: Corn, soybeans, wheat, and carrots are almost always direct seeded.
segments.tr: El maíz, la soja, el trigo y las zanahorias casi siempre se siembran directamente.

segments.src: It's cheap and fast — a planter can cover 40 acres an hour — but the seed is on its own out there, exposed to cold soil, crusting, birds, and weeds that germinate at the same time.
segments.tr: Es barato y rápido — una sembradora puede cubrir 40 acres por hora — pero la semilla está sola allí, expuesta al suelo frío, encostramiento, pájaros y malezas que germinan al mismo tiempo.

segments.src: **Transplanting** means the seed germinates somewhere controlled — a greenhouse tray, a nursery bed — and the young plant is moved into the field later.
segments.tr: **El trasplante** significa que la semilla germina en algún lugar controlado — una bandeja de invernadero, un lecho de vivero — y la planta joven se traslada al campo más tarde.

segments.src: Tomatoes, peppers, broccoli, strawberries, and rice (in much of the world) go this route.
segments.tr: Los tomates, pimientos, brócoli, fresas y arroz (en gran parte del mundo) siguen esta ruta.

segments.src: The controlled stage is called **raising seedlings**, or *nursery raising*.
segments.tr: La etapa controlada se llama **crianza de plántulas**, o *producción en vivero*.

segments.src: It costs far more per plant, but it buys you three things:
segments.tr: Cuesta mucho más por planta, pero te compra tres cosas:

segments.src: 1. **Time.** The seedling grows in a warm greenhouse in March while the field is still frozen. When you set it out in May, it's already five weeks old. In a short-season state like Minnesota, that's the difference between harvesting and not.
segments.tr: 1. **Tiempo.** La plántula crece en un invernadero cálido en marzo mientras el campo sigue congelado. Cuando la pones afuera en mayo, ya tiene cinco semanas. En un estado de temporada corta como Minnesota, esa es la diferencia entre cosechar y no hacerlo.

segments.src: 2. **Uniformity.** You throw away the weak seedlings before they ever occupy field space. A direct-seeded field carries its runts all season.
segments.tr: 2. **Uniformidad.** Desechas las plántulas débiles antes de que ocupen espacio de campo. Un campo sembrado directamente lleva sus plantas débiles toda la temporada.

segments.src: 3. **A head start on weeds.** A four-week-old transplant shades out weed seedlings that a germinating direct-seeded crop would lose to.
segments.tr: 3. **Una ventaja contra las malezas.** Un trasplante de cuatro semanas sombrea las plántulas de malezas a las que sucumbiría un cultivo de siembra directa que recién germina.

segments.src: The cost is **transplant shock** — roots get disturbed, the plant sulks for a few days.
segments.tr: El costo es **choque de trasplante** — las raíces se disturban, la planta se deprime durante algunos días.

segments.src: The standard fix is **hardening off**: a week or so of gradually exposing seedlings to outdoor cold, wind, and full sun so they toughen up before the move.
segments.tr: La solución estándar es **endurecimiento**: una semana más o menos de exponer gradualmente las plántulas al frío, viento y sol pleno para que se endurezcan antes del traslado.

segments.src: Then comes the third decision: **planting density** — how many plants per acre, and how they're arranged.
segments.tr: Luego viene la tercera decisión: **densidad de siembra** — cuántas plantas por acre, y cómo están distribuidas.

segments.src: This is the one that surprises people.
segments.tr: Esta es la que sorprende a la gente.

segments.src: More plants does *not* mean more yield forever.
segments.tr: Más plantas *no* significan más rendimiento para siempre.

segments.src: As you crowd plants together:
segments.tr: A medida que amontonas las plantas:

segments.src: - **Yield per acre** rises, plateaus, and then falls (lodging, disease, shading).
segments.tr: - **Rendimiento por acre** sube, se estabiliza, y luego baja (acame, enfermedad, sombreado).

segments.src: - **Yield per individual plant** falls the whole way — steadily, from the very first added plant.
segments.tr: - **Rendimiento por planta individual** baja todo el camino — constantemente, desde la primera planta agregada.

segments.src: Which curve you optimize for depends on what you're selling.
segments.tr: Qué curva optimizas depende de qué estés vendiendo.

segments.src: If you sell by the ton — corn silage, hay, processing tomatoes — push density high and don't care that each plant is smaller.
segments.tr: Si vendes por tonelada — ensilaje de maíz, heno, tomates para procesamiento — aumenta la densidad y no te importa que cada planta sea más pequeña.

segments.src: If you sell by the unit and size matters — a head of cabbage, a jack-o'-lantern pumpkin, a table-grade apple — back off, because a field of undersized product is worth less than a field of fewer good ones.
segments.tr: Si vendes por unidad y el tamaño importa — una cabeza de repollo, una calabaza de jack-o'-lantern, una manzana de calidad de mesa — retrocede, porque un campo lleno de producto de tamaño insuficiente vale menos que un campo con menos plantas pero de buen tamaño.

segments.src: The arrangement matters too, not just the count.
segments.tr: La disposición también importa, no solo la cantidad.

segments.src: The same 30,000 plants per acre can sit in 30-inch rows or 15-inch rows.
segments.tr: Las mismas 30,000 plantas por acre pueden estar en filas de 30 pulgadas o filas de 15 pulgadas.

segments.src: Narrower rows spread plants into a more even, square-ish spacing, so each one competes less with its immediate neighbors and the canopy closes over the soil sooner — which shades out weeds and keeps moisture in.
segments.tr: Las filas más estrechas distribuyen las plantas en un espaciamiento más uniforme y cuadrangular, por lo que cada una compite menos con sus vecinos inmediatos y el dosel se cierra sobre el suelo más rápido — lo que sombrea las malezas y mantiene la humedad.

segments.src: That's a big part of why US corn row spacing narrowed over the last century, alongside breeding for plants that tolerate crowding.
segments.tr: Esa es una gran parte de por qué el espaciamiento de filas de maíz en EE.UU. se estrechó durante el siglo pasado, junto con la reproducción de plantas que toleran el hacinamiento.

segments.src: Rough shape of the relationship, in plain text:
segments.tr: Forma aproximada de la relación, en texto plano:

segments.src: plants per acre = 43,560 / (row spacing in ft x in-row spacing in ft)
segments.tr: plants per acre = 43,560 / (row spacing in ft x in-row spacing in ft)

segments.src: So 30-inch rows (2.5 ft) with plants 7 inches apart in the row (0.583 ft) gives about 43,560 / 1.458 ≈ 29,900 plants per acre.
segments.tr: Así que filas de 30 pulgadas (2.5 ft) con plantas de 7 pulgadas de separación en la fila (0.583 ft) da aproximadamente 43,560 / 1.458 ≈ 29,900 plantas por acre.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## En la vida cotidiana

segments.src: Walk through a garden center in Ohio in late April and you're looking at the whole lesson on two tables.
segments.tr: Camina por un centro de jardinería en Ohio a finales de abril y estás mirando toda la lección en dos mesas.

segments.src: On one table: seed packets.
segments.tr: En una mesa: paquetes de semillas.

segments.src: Beans, sweet corn, radishes, carrots — $2 to $4 a packet, dozens of seeds each.
segments.tr: Frijoles, maíz dulce, rábanos, zanahorias — $2 a $4 por paquete, docenas de semillas cada uno.

segments.src: These are the direct-seed crops.
segments.tr: Estos son los cultivos de siembra directa.

segments.src: The packet says "sow directly outdoors after last frost" because these plants either grow fast enough not to need a head start (radishes, 25 days) or hate having their roots disturbed (carrots, beans).
segments.tr: El paquete dice "siembra directamente al aire libre después de la última helada" porque estas plantas o crecen lo suficientemente rápido para no necesitar una ventaja inicial (rábanos, 25 días) u odian tener sus raíces perturbadas (zanahorias, frijoles).

segments.src: On the other table: cell packs of tomato and pepper starts, $4 to $6 for a four-pack.
segments.tr: En la otra mesa: bandejas de plantas de tomates y pimientos, $4 a $6 por un paquete de cuatro.

segments.src: Nobody sells tomato seed packets to casual buyers with a straight face in Ohio, because a tomato seeded outdoors in May in Columbus won't ripen before the first fall frost.
segments.tr: Nadie vende paquetes de semillas de tomate a compradores casuales con seriedad en Ohio, porque un tomate sembrado al aire libre en mayo en Columbus no madurará antes de la primera helada de otoño.

segments.src: Somebody already did the nursery-raising work in February in a heated greenhouse — that's what you're paying for, and it's why a single tomato plant costs more than an entire packet of bean seed.
segments.tr: Alguien ya hizo el trabajo de crianza en vivero en febrero en un invernadero calefaccionado — eso es por lo que estás pagando, y es por qué una sola planta de tomate cuesta más que un paquete completo de semillas de frijol.

segments.src: Now the density part.
segments.tr: Ahora la parte de densidad.

segments.src: Flip over that tomato tag: "space 24-36 inches apart."
segments.tr: Lee la etiqueta del tomate: "espaciar 24-36 pulgadas de distancia."

segments.src: Most first-time gardeners ignore it and plant six tomatoes in a 4x4 raised bed, because the transplants look tiny and the bed looks empty.
segments.tr: La mayoría de los jardineros primerizos lo ignoran y plantan seis tomates en una cama elevada de 4x4, porque los trasplantes se ven diminutos y la cama se ve vacía.

segments.src: By August they've got a tangled mat with poor air circulation, more disease, and small fruit — a personal-scale demonstration of the yield-per-plant curve.
segments.tr: Para agosto tienen una maraña enredada con pobre circulación de aire, más enfermedad y fruta pequeña — una demostración a escala personal de la curva de rendimiento por planta.

segments.src: The commercial grower down the road faces the identical tradeoff, just with a spreadsheet: a processing tomato field headed for a cannery gets crowded hard, because the plant is selling by the ton.
segments.tr: El productor comercial cercano enfrenta el mismo tradeoff, solo que con una hoja de cálculo: un campo de tomate para procesamiento dirigido a una enlatadora se amontonan mucho, porque la planta se vende por tonelada.

segments.src: A fresh-market field where big, blemish-free fruit brings a premium at the farmers market in Athens gets more room per plant.
segments.tr: Un campo de mercado fresco donde la fruta grande y sin defectos obtiene una prima en el mercado de agricultores en Athens obtiene más espacio por planta.

segments.src: Same crop.
segments.tr: Mismo cultivo.

segments.src: Different market.
segments.tr: Mercado diferente.

segments.src: Different correct density.
segments.tr: Densidad correcta diferente.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Resumen de tres líneas

segments.src: 1. Direct seeding puts seed straight in the field — cheap and fast; transplanting raises seedlings in a controlled nursery first — expensive, but it buys season length, uniformity, and a weed head start.
segments.tr: 1. La siembra directa pone la semilla directamente en el campo — barato y rápido; el trasplante cría plántulas en un vivero controlado primero — costoso, pero te compra duración de temporada, uniformidad y una ventaja contra las malezas.

segments.src: 2. As planting density rises, yield per acre goes up then eventually down, while yield per individual plant declines the entire time — so the right density depends on whether your market pays by weight or by the size of each unit.
segments.tr: 2. A medida que aumenta la densidad de siembra, el rendimiento por acre sube y luego eventualmente baja, mientras que el rendimiento por planta individual disminuye todo el tiempo — así que la densidad correcta depende de si tu mercado paga por peso o por el tamaño de cada unidad.

segments.src: 3. Arrangement matters alongside count: narrower rows spread the same plant population more evenly, reducing crowding between neighbors and closing the canopy sooner.
segments.tr: 3. La disposición importa junto con la cantidad: las filas más estrechas distribuyen la misma población de plantas más uniformemente, reduciendo el hacinamiento entre vecinos y cerrando el dosel más rápido.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Términos de hoy

segments.src: - **Direct seeding** — sowing seed straight into the field where the crop will grow to maturity, with no nursery stage.
segments.tr: - **Siembra directa** — sembrar la semilla directamente en el campo donde el cultivo crecerá hasta la madurez, sin etapa de vivero.

segments.src: - **Transplanting** — moving a plant started elsewhere (greenhouse, nursery bed) into its final field position.
segments.tr: - **Trasplante** — mover una planta iniciada en otro lugar (invernadero, lecho de vivero) a su posición de campo final.

segments.src: - **Nursery raising (seedling production)** — growing young plants under controlled conditions before field setting, to gain season length and uniformity.
segments.tr: - **Crianza en vivero (producción de plántulas)** — cultivar plantas jóvenes bajo condiciones controladas antes de establecerlas en el campo, para ganar duración de temporada y uniformidad.

segments.src: - **Hardening off** — gradually acclimating protected seedlings to outdoor cold, wind, and sun so they survive transplanting with less shock.
segments.tr: - **Endurecimiento** — aclimatar gradualmente las plántulas protegidas al frío, viento y sol exterior para que sobrevivan al trasplante con menos choque.

segments.src: - **Planting density (plant population)** — the number of plants per unit area, usually stated as plants per acre.
segments.tr: - **Densidad de siembra (población de plantas)** — el número de plantas por unidad de área, generalmente expresado como plantas por acre.

segments.src: - **Transplant shock** — the temporary growth setback a plant suffers from root disturbance and environmental change during transplanting.
segments.tr: - **Choque de trasplante** — el retroceso temporal de crecimiento que sufre una planta por perturbación de raíces y cambio ambiental durante el trasplante.

segments.tr: إنه رخيص وسريع — يمكن للزارع أن يغطي 40 فدان في الساعة — لكن البذرة وحدها هناك، معرضة للتربة الباردة والقشرة والطيور والأعشاب التي تنبت في نفس الوقت.

segments.src: **Transplanting** means the seed germinates somewhere controlled — a greenhouse tray, a nursery bed — and the young plant is moved into the field later.
segments.tr: **الزراعة بالشتل** تعني أن البذرة تنبت في مكان مضبوط — صينية بيت زجاجي، سرير مشتل — والنبات الصغير يُنقل إلى الحقل لاحقاً.

segments.src: Tomatoes, peppers, broccoli, strawberries, and rice (in much of the world) go this route.
segments.tr: الطماطم والفلفل والبروكلي والفراولة والأرز (في معظم أنحاء العالم) تتبع هذا الطريق.

segments.src: The controlled stage is called **raising seedlings**, or *nursery raising*.
segments.tr: المرحلة المضبوطة تُسمى **تربية الشتلات**، أو *تربية المشتل*.

segments.src: It costs far more per plant, but it buys you three things:
segments.tr: إنها تكلف أكثر بكثير لكل نبات، لكنها تشتري لك ثلاثة أشياء:

segments.src: 1. **Time.** The seedling grows in a warm greenhouse in March while the field is still frozen. When you set it out in May, it's already five weeks old. In a short-season state like Minnesota, that's the difference between harvesting and not.
segments.tr: 1. **الوقت.** تنمو الشتلة في بيت زجاجي دافئ في مارس بينما الحقل لا يزال مجمداً. عندما تضعها في مايو، تكون قد أمضت خمسة أسابيع. في ولاية قصيرة الموسم مثل مينيسوتا، هذا هو الفرق بين الحصاد أم لا.

segments.src: 2. **Uniformity.** You throw away the weak seedlings before they ever occupy field space. A direct-seeded field carries its runts all season.
segments.tr: 2. **التوحيد.** تتخلص من الشتلات الضعيفة قبل أن تحتل مساحة حقل. الحقل المبذور مباشرة يحمل الضعفاء طوال الموسم.

segments.src: 3. **A head start on weeds.** A four-week-old transplant shades out weed seedlings that a germinating direct-seeded crop would lose to.
segments.tr: 3. **بداية متقدمة ضد الأعشاب.** الشتلة التي تبلغ من العمر أربعة أسابيع تظلل شتلات الأعشاب التي كانت محصول مبذور مباشر سيخسرها.

segments.src: The cost is **transplant shock** — roots get disturbed, the plant sulks for a few days.
segments.tr: التكلفة هي **صدمة الزراعة بالشتل** — تتعطل الجذور، والنبات يتذمر لعدة أيام.

segments.src: The standard fix is **hardening off**: a week or so of gradually exposing seedlings to outdoor cold, wind, and full sun so they toughen up before the move.
segments.tr: الإصلاح القياسي هو **تقسية الشتلات**: حوالي أسبوع من تعريض الشتلات تدريجياً للبرد والرياح وأشعة الشمس الكاملة بالخارج لتقويتها قبل الانتقال.

segments.src: Then comes the third decision: **planting density** — how many plants per acre, and how they're arranged.
segments.tr: ثم يأتي القرار الثالث: **كثافة الزراعة** — كم عدد النباتات لكل فدان، وكيف يتم ترتيبها.

segments.src: This is the one that surprises people.
segments.tr: هذا هو الذي يفاجئ الناس.

segments.src: More plants does *not* mean more yield forever.
segments.tr: المزيد من النباتات لا يعني المزيد من الحصاد إلى الأبد.

segments.src: As you crowd plants together:
segments.tr: عندما تزحم النباتات معاً:

segments.src: - **Yield per acre** rises, plateaus, and then falls (lodging, disease, shading).
segments.tr: - **المحصول لكل فدان** يرتفع، ويصل إلى هضبة، ثم ينخفض (الرقود، المرض، الظل).

segments.src: - **Yield per individual plant** falls the whole way — steadily, from the very first added plant.
segments.tr: - **المحصول لكل نبات فردي** ينخفض طوال الوقت — بثبات، من النبات المضاف الأول جداً.

segments.src: Which curve you optimize for depends on what you're selling.
segments.tr: أي منحنى تحسنه يعتمد على ما تبيعه.

segments.src: If you sell by the ton — corn silage, hay, processing tomatoes — push density high and don't care that each plant is smaller.
segments.tr: إذا كنت تبيع بالطن — سيلاج الذرة، القش، الطماطم المصنعة — ادفع الكثافة عالية ولا تهتم بأن كل نبات أصغر.

segments.src: If you sell by the unit and size matters — a head of cabbage, a jack-o'-lantern pumpkin, a table-grade apple — back off, because a field of undersized product is worth less than a field of fewer good ones.
segments.tr: إذا كنت تبيع بالوحدة والحجم مهم — رأس ملفوف، قرع فانوس جاك، تفاحة من فئة الطاولة — تراجع، لأن حقل المنتجات الصغيرة يساوي أقل من حقل من الأشياء الجيدة الأقل عدداً.

segments.src: The arrangement matters too, not just the count.
segments.tr: الترتيب مهم أيضاً، وليس فقط العدد.

segments.src: The same 30,000 plants per acre can sit in 30-inch rows or 15-inch rows.
segments.tr: نفس 30000 نبات لكل فدان يمكن أن تجلس في صفوف 30 بوصة أو 15 بوصة.

segments.src: Narrower rows spread plants into a more even, square-ish spacing, so each one competes less with its immediate neighbors and the canopy closes over the soil sooner — which shades out weeds and keeps moisture in.
segments.tr: الصفوف الأضيق تنشر النباتات إلى تباعد أكثر توازناً وربع شكل، لذا يتنافس كل واحد أقل مع جيرانه الفوريين والمظلة تغلق على التربة بشكل أسرع — مما يظلل الأعشاب ويحافظ على الرطوبة.

segments.src: That's a big part of why US corn row spacing narrowed over the last century, alongside breeding for plants that tolerate crowding.
segments.tr: هذا جزء كبير من سبب تضييق تباعد صفوف الذرة في الولايات المتحدة على مدى القرن الماضي، إلى جانب التربية للنباتات التي تتحمل الازدحام.

segments.src: Rough shape of the relationship, in plain text:
segments.tr: شكل تقريبي للعلاقة، في نص عادي:

segments.src: plants per acre = 43,560 / (row spacing in ft x in-row spacing in ft)
segments.tr: plants per acre = 43,560 / (row spacing in ft x in-row spacing in ft)

segments.src: So 30-inch rows (2.5 ft) with plants 7 inches apart in the row (0.583 ft) gives about 43,560 / 1.458 ≈ 29,900 plants per acre.
segments.tr: إذاً صفوف 30 بوصة (2.5 قدم) مع نباتات تباعدها 7 بوصات في الصف (0.583 قدم) تعطي حوالي 43,560 / 1.458 ≈ 29,900 نبات لكل فدان.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## في الحياة اليومية

segments.src: Walk through a garden center in Ohio in late April and you're looking at the whole lesson on two tables.
segments.tr: امشِ عبر مركز حديقة في أوهايو في أواخر أبريل وأنت تنظر إلى الدرس كله على طاولتين.

segments.src: On one table: seed packets.
segments.tr: على طاولة واحدة: علب البذور.

segments.src: Beans, sweet corn, radishes, carrots — $2 to $4 a packet, dozens of seeds each.
segments.tr: الفاصوليا، الذرة الحلوة، الفجل، الجزر — 2 إلى 4 دولارات لكل علبة، عشرات البذور لكل واحدة.

segments.src: These are the direct-seed crops.
segments.tr: هذه هي محاصيل البذر المباشر.

segments.src: The packet says "sow directly outdoors after last frost" because these plants either grow fast enough not to need a head start (radishes, 25 days) or hate having their roots disturbed (carrots, beans).
segments.tr: تقول العبوة "ازرع مباشرة في الهواء الطلق بعد آخر صقيع" لأن هذه النباتات إما تنمو بسرعة كافية لعدم الحاجة إلى بداية متقدمة (الفجل، 25 يوماً) أو تكره إزعاج جذورها (الجزر، الفاصوليا).

segments.src: On the other table: cell packs of tomato and pepper starts, $4 to $6 for a four-pack.
segments.tr: على الطاولة الأخرى: عبوات خلايا من شتلات الطماطم والفلفل، 4 إلى 6 دولارات لكل حزمة من أربعة.

segments.src: Nobody sells tomato seed packets to casual buyers with a straight face in Ohio, because a tomato seeded outdoors in May in Columbus won't ripen before the first fall frost.
segments.tr: لا أحد يبيع علب بذور الطماطم لعامة الناس برصانة في أوهايو، لأن الطماطم المبذورة في الهواء الطلق في مايو في كولومبوس لن تنضج قبل أول صقيع الخريف.

segments.src: Somebody already did the nursery-raising work in February in a heated greenhouse — that's what you're paying for, and it's why a single tomato plant costs more than an entire packet of bean seed.
segments.tr: شخص ما قام بالفعل بعمل تربية المشتل في فبراير في بيت زجاجي مدفأ — هذا ما تدفع ثمنه، وهذا السبب في أن نبات طماطم واحد يكلف أكثر من علبة كاملة من بذور الفاصوليا.

segments.src: Now the density part.
segments.tr: الآن جزء الكثافة.

segments.src: Flip over that tomato tag: "space 24-36 inches apart."
segments.tr: اقلب بطاقة الطماطم: "تباعد 24-36 بوصة بعضها عن بعض."

segments.src: Most first-time gardeners ignore it and plant six tomatoes in a 4x4 raised bed, because the transplants look tiny and the bed looks empty.
segments.tr: معظم بستانيي المبتدئين يتجاهلونها ويزرعون ستة طماطم في سرير مرتفع 4x4، لأن الشتلات تبدو صغيرة والسرير يبدو فارغاً.

segments.src: By August they've got a tangled mat with poor air circulation, more disease, and small fruit — a personal-scale demonstration of the yield-per-plant curve.
segments.tr: بحلول أغسطس، لديهم حصيرة متشابكة بتهوية ضعيفة، ومزيد من المرض، وفاكهة صغيرة — عرض على نطاق شخصي لمنحنى المحصول لكل نبات.

segments.src: The commercial grower down the road faces the identical tradeoff, just with a spreadsheet: a processing tomato field headed for a cannery gets crowded hard, because the plant is selling by the ton.
segments.tr: يواجه المزارع التجاري في الطريق نفس المقايضة، فقط مع جدول بيانات: حقل الطماطم المصنعة الموجه لمعمل تعليب يُزحم بشدة، لأن النبات يُباع بالطن.

segments.src: A fresh-market field where big, blemish-free fruit brings a premium at the farmers market in Athens gets more room per plant.
segments.tr: حقل السوق الطازج حيث الثمار الكبيرة والخالية من العيوب تحقق قسطاً في سوق المزارعين في أثينا يحصل على مساحة أكثر لكل نبات.

segments.src: Same crop.
segments.tr: نفس المحصول.

segments.src: Different market.
segments.tr: سوق مختلف.

segments.src: Different correct density.
segments.tr: كثافة مختلفة صحيحة.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## ملخص من ثلاثة أسطر

segments.src: 1. Direct seeding puts seed straight in the field — cheap and fast; transplanting raises seedlings in a controlled nursery first — expensive, but it buys season length, uniformity, and a weed head start.
segments.tr: 1. البذر المباشر يضع البذرة مباشرة في الحقل — رخيص وسريع؛ والزراعة بالشتل تربي الشتلات في مشتل مضبوط أولاً — مكلفة، لكنها تشتري طول الموسم والتوحيد والبداية المتقدمة للأعشاب.

segments.src: 2. As planting density rises, yield per acre goes up then eventually down, while yield per individual plant declines the entire time — so the right density depends on whether your market pays by weight or by the size of each unit.
segments.tr: 2. مع ارتفاع كثافة الزراعة، يرتفع المحصول لكل فدان ثم ينخفض في النهاية، بينما المحصول لكل نبات فردي ينخفض طوال الوقت — لذا الكثافة الصحيحة تعتمد على ما إذا كان سوقك يدفع بالوزن أو بحجم كل وحدة.

segments.src: 3. Arrangement matters alongside count: narrower rows spread the same plant population more evenly, reducing crowding between neighbors and closing the canopy sooner.
segments.tr: 3. الترتيب مهم إلى جانب العدد: الصفوف الأضيق تنشر نفس عدد السكان النباتي بشكل أكثر توازناً، مما يقلل الازدحام بين الجيران وإغلاق المظلة بشكل أسرع.

segments.tr: ## ✅ اختبار ذاتي

segments.src: As you increase planting density, what happens to yield per individual plant?**
segments.tr: مع زيادة كثافة الزراعة، ما الذي يحدث لمحصول كل نبات فردي؟**

segments.src: - A) It rises, then falls
segments.tr: - أ) يرتفع، ثم ينخفض

segments.src: - B) It falls steadily throughout
segments.tr: - ب) ينخفض بثبات طوال الوقت

segments.src: - C) It stays flat until the field is overcrowded
segments.tr: - ج) يبقى مسطحاً حتى يكون الحقل مكتظاً

segments.src: - D) It rises steadily throughout
segments.tr: - د) يرتفع بثبات طوال الوقت

segments.src: "Hardening off" refers to:**
segments.tr: تقسية الشتلات" تشير إلى:**

segments.src: - A) Letting soil dry and crust before planting
segments.tr: - أ) ترك التربة تجف وتقسو قبل الزراعة

segments.src: - B) Selecting only the strongest seeds before sowing
segments.tr: - ب) اختيار البذور الأقوى فقط قبل البذر

segments.src: - C) Gradually exposing greenhouse seedlings to outdoor conditions before transplanting
segments.tr: - ج) تعريض شتلات بيت زجاجي تدريجياً للظروف الخارجية قبل الزراعة بالشتل

segments.src: - D) Compacting soil around the roots after transplanting
segments.tr: - د) دك التربة حول الجذور بعد الزراعة بالشتل
